headline: Approved utility lien waivers, Foss Road acquisition, HOME budget, and postponed ethics policy and railroad dissolution.
summary: The Council approved several orders including a forfeiture funds transfer, a traffic schedule change on Bates Street, utility lien foreclosure waivers for distressed structures on leased land, a public hearing date for City Charter amendments, a Planning Board appointment, the amended HOME Budget and Action Plan for HUD, and the acquisition of a 1.44 acre portion of 9 Foss Road. The Council postponed action on amendments to the Ethics Policy and postponed indefinitely an order to explore dissolving the Lewiston Auburn Railroad Company. A public hearing was also held on the Lewiston Falls Hydroelectric Project relicensing, and the Council entered executive session to discuss a legal matter and real estate.
decisions: Approved the transfer of forfeiture funds from two court cases to the City of Lewiston Drug Enforcement Program account.
Approved an amendment to the Traffic Schedule to add two-hour parking on a portion of Bates Street.
Approved waiving utility lien foreclosure on eleven distressed structures located on leased land.
Approved calling for a public hearing on September 1 regarding proposed City Charter amendments.
Appointed Darren Gallant to the Planning Board, term to expire January 2, 2029.
Postponed the proposed amendments to the Ethics Policy, City Policy Manual Number 94, to a future workshop.
Approved the amended City FY27 (Federal FY2026) HOME Budget and Action Plan, totaling $1,195,374.04 for Lewiston, for submittal to HUD.
Postponed indefinitely the order directing the City Administrator to explore dissolution of the Lewiston Auburn Railroad Company.
Approved the acquisition of a 1.44 acre portion of 9 Foss Road for $35,000 to construct a bypass road.

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
 
REGULAR MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 7:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Roy, Noble, Chittim, 
and Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath, Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley, and 
City Clerk Kathleen Montejo.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
VOTE (299-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To dispense with the reading of the minutes of the meeting of August 4, 2026, and to accept and 
place them on file as prepared by the City Clerk.   Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
Ronnie Paradis, Ward 6 – Please talk about issues and not people. Who will protect the mobile 
unit when it goes out into homeless encampments? The violence and shootings are still 
happening. Bangor has cases of HIV that are spreading quickly, the unhoused situation is out of 
control there. 
 
Melissa Dunn, Blake St – There are classes of racism at City Hall and the Police Department 
with civic and human rights violations. Members of the Police Department and family members 
of Councilors have cyber stalked her. Her rights to observe activities in public have been 
violated, the officers on the streets need better training. 
 
John Horton, Ward 2 – Opposed to the mobile home rent control ordinance. The ordinance, 
while well-intended, will not work. Park owners have expenses such as plowing, insurance, 
maintenance, etc, this ordinance will create a loss for them. The average lot rent in Lewiston is 
$502 a month. There isn’t a problem in Lewiston, the park owners are not the problem.  
 
Chris Saroie – Lewiston mobile home park owner – If the income for parks is restricted, will 
have to cut reserved funds dedicated for future improvements such as cutting back brush, etc.  
Lot rent increases are low compared to other household expenses that have skyrocketed such as 
groceries, gas, oil, healthcare, etc. 
 
Destiny Johnson, Windham and Lewiston shooting survivor – 18 people lost lives in mass 
shooting, public safety is supposed to be a priority for the Council.  People expect accountability 
from the agencies that received funding what should have gone to the families of victims and 
survivors. Mayor is a board member of the Maine Mill which received $65,000 
 
Christine Holden, Ward 1 – The sidewalks and roads that have been recently paved look nice.  
At the one month mark of the new trash can program, the city should evaluate the success.
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
2 
 
Concerns with electric bikes that are driving on the roads, not signaling, moving in between 
vehicles. 
 
Nathan Pearl, Lewiston – This country has been able to build skyscrapers for 141 years but here 
are 800,000 unhoused residents in this country that are suffering and the effect is viewed locally. 
 
Kim Bush, Ward 2 – Stores are open until midnight, but patrons are getting hurt from customers 
with mental health issues.  The Calgary Methodist church is ending their food program, where 
will people go? Can the city provide funding for the program to continue?  
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – What is the status of the third floor reorganization program?  Has talked 
with residents, people do not feel safe coming downtown to attend Council meetings. Social 
media magnifies the issues and scares people away. 
 
Ifraax Saciid-Ciise, Lewiston translated for Hola Noor – Was ill for three days, did not leave her 
home, parked car in lot close to house.  Received a ticket for not moving and said the car would 
be towed.  It is not a snowstorm, no reason to have it removed.  
 
 
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT 
 
The City Administrator reported the new Casella trash cans will be distributed starting on August 
24. The Community Ambassadors program kicked off last week with 40 volunteers. The Balloon 
Festival will be held on August 21-23.  Director of Social Service Elaine Brackett has 40 years 
of city service. The Department of Economic and Community Development will be rolling out 
new loan programs. The 1820 Spirits company Lewiston plant has been named the best plant in 
the company. The next Meet & Greet will be held at the Clarion Inn on August 20 for residents 
of Ward 7 and Councilor Martel will be present.  
 
AUTHORIZATION TO ACCEPT TRANSFER OF FORFEITURE FUNDS 
 
VOTE (300-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That pursuant to Title 15, Maine Revised Statutes Annotated, Section 5824(3) and Section 
5822(4)(A), the City Council hereby acknowledges and approves the transfer of $2,340.00 or any 
portion thereof, in the case of the State of Maine vs. David Mockler, Do cket Number ANDCD-
CR-2022-00625 and the transfer of $1,385.00 or any portion thereof, in the case of the State of 
Maine vs. James Roseney Docket Number ANDCD-CR-2022-02148 Court Records, being funds 
forfeited pursuant to the court process. It is further acknowledged that these funds shall be credited 
to the ‘City of Lewiston Drug Enforcement Program’ account. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
AMENDMENT TO THE TRAFFIC SCHEDULE TO ADD TWO-HOUR PARKING ON 
A PORTION OF BATES STREET
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
3 
 
VOTE (301-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve an Amendment to the Traffic Schedule to add additional parking spaces on a portion 
of Bates Street for Parking Time Regulated, Monday through Friday, 2-hours 9:00 AM to 6:00 
PM and amend Section 48 Busses Only Parking to accommodate this addition, as outlined in the 
attached vote sheet.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING EXECUTION OF WAIVING UTILITY LIEN 
FORECLOSURE ON CERTAIN DISTRESSED STRUCTURES ON LEASED LAND 
ORDER, AUTHORIZING THE APPLICATION AND ACCEPTANCE OF FUNDS 
FROM THE MAINE BUREAU OF HIGHWAY SAFETY 
 
VOTE (302-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To approve the Order, Authorizing execution of waiving utility lien foreclosure on certain 
distressed structures on leased land: 
 
Whereas, the City has a long and successful history of working with property owners who 
have difficulty meeting their utility charge obligations; and 
 
Whereas, utility liens automatically mature on property on which utility charges have not been 
paid eighteen months after the City files liens against them; and 
 
Whereas, once liens mature, the City becomes the technical owner of these properties; and 
 
Whereas, this process is established by State Law to ensure that the City is paid the utility charges  
owed, at which time the property is normally returned to its prior owner; and 
 
Whereas, if a property on which a lien has matured is abandoned by its prior owner for a period of  
60 days, the City may become liable for costs associated with the demolition and removal of  
distressed structures and/or any claims for damages that might arise as a result of the condition of,  
or hazards posed by the property; and 
 
Whereas, in certain instances, especially where structures are located on leased land, the City may  
be unable to recover back utility charges and demolition or other costs associated with such  
properties; and 
 
Whereas, in such instances, it may be in the best interest of the City to waive foreclosure while  
alternatives are sought to address these problem properties, including working with property and  
leased-land owners; and 
 
Whereas, a number of distressed structures located on leased land on which liens will mature on  
August 20, 2026 have been identified; and 
 
Whereas, it is in the best interest of the City that foreclosure on these structures be waived;
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
4

Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, CALLING FOR A PUBLIC HEARING FOR THE PROPOSED CITY 
CHARTER AMENDMENTS 
 
VOTE (303-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
  
To approve the Order, Calling for a Public Hearing for the proposed City Charter amendments: 
 
Whereas, The City Council has authorized over the past few months three amendments to the 
City Charter to appear on the November ballot, and 
Whereas, Maine state statutes require a public hearing to be held before election day regarding 
the amendments, and
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
5 
 
Whereas, The statutes require a legal advertisement to run at least seven days before the public 
hearing,  
Now, Therefore, Be It Ordered by the City Council that the City Council calls for a public 
hearing on the proposed Charter amendments to be held on September 1 and directs city staff to 
place the necessary legal notice as prescribed by state statutes.  
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
APPOINTMENT TO THE PLANNING BOARD 
 
VOTE (304-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To confirm the Mayor’s nomination and to appoint the following resident as a member of the 
Planning Board:  Darren Gallant, 4 Benson Street, term to expire January 2, 2029  
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC HEARING REGARDING THE LEWISTON FALLS HYDROELECTRIC 
PROJECT FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION RELICENSING 
 
Public Works Director Kevin Gagne and Director of Planning & Code Enforcement Jon Connor 
made a presentation to the Council regarding the background and history of this issue. 
The Mayor opened the public hearing to receive input from the public regarding the proposed 
relicensing of the Lewiston Falls Hydroelectric Project. Matt Roy, Ward 6 – Last December, the 
Council voted down an AI Datacenter. This hearing is now being held days before the report is 
due. This should have been brought to the public’s attention months ago. Christine Holden, Ward 
1 – Access to recreation on the river is important and is outlined in the city’s Comprehensive 
Plan.  
 
AMENDMENTS TO THE CITY’S ETHICS POLICY, POLICY MANUAL NUMBER 94 
 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Longchamps: 
 
To approve the proposed amendments to the Ethics Policy, City Policy Manual Number 94. 
 
VOTE (305-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Martel, seconded by Councilor Noble: 
 
To postpone this item to a future workshop.  Passed - Vote 6-1 (Councilor Longchamps 
opposed) 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE AMENDED CITY FY27 (FEDERAL FY2026) HOME 
BUDGET AND ACTION PLAN FOR SUBMITTAL TO THE US DEPARTMENT OF 
HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT (HUD) 
 
VOTE (306-2026)
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
6 
 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To Adopt the Order, Approving the Amended City FY27 (Federal FY2026) HOME Budget and 
Action Plan for submittal to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD): 
 
Whereas, on May 5, 2026 after holding a workshop on March 17, 2026 and two public hearings  
on April 7, 2026 and May 5, 2026, and not receiving any comments, the City Council adopted a  
HOME Budget and Action Plan for the City’s FY27 (Federal FY2026) upon recommendation of  
the Community Development Citizen Advisory Committee on how Lewiston’s share of the  
Auburn Lewiston HOME Consortium FY27 proposed allocation and the previous year’s funding  
to be rolled forward would be invested; and 
 
Whereas, the City has been notified of the final Consortium Budget for FY27 (Federal FY2026)  
which has been approved by HUD at $484,730.26 and is to be divided between Lewiston and  
Auburn; and  
 
Whereas, the amended HOME Budget for FY27 (Federal FY2026) is $1,195,374.04 for Lewiston  
which is an increase of $2,614.37 or .22% over last year’s budget; and  
 
Whereas, HUD requires local acceptance of the amended HOME Budget and Action Plan   
resulting in the grant; and 
 
Now, therefore, be it Ordered by the City Council of the City of Lewiston that the Amended  
HOME Budget and Action Plan for City FY27 (Federal FY2026) is hereby approved and  
authorized to be submitted to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development. 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, DIRECTING THE CITY ADMINISTRATOR TO EXPLORE THE 
DISSOLUTION OF THE LEWISTON AUBURN RAILROAD COMPANY 
 
VOTE (307-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To postpone this matter indefinitely.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
ORDER, APPROVING THE ACQUISITION OF A 1.44 ACRE PORTION OF 
9 FOSS ROAD 
 
VOTE (308-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To approve the Order, Approving the Acquisition of a 1.44 acre portion of 9 Foss Road: 
 
Whereas, Jordan Road Bridge was identified as deficient by Maine DOT in 2021 due to voids in  
the stone abutments and erosion at the corners; and
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
7 
 
Whereas, the bridge was constructed in 1966 and rehabilitated in 2002 and services four residents  
and multiple vacant parcels; and 
 
Whereas, the bridge is identified as scour critical such that it needs to be closed when flood waters  
reach a certain level and as a dead end road there is no alternative access for residents except  
through the Vineyard Pathways Church parking lot; and 
 
Whereas, there is an existing public crossing over No Name Brook 250 feet upstream on Foss Rd;  
And 
 
Whereas, engineering studies have recommended that repairs to the bridge would only be  
temporary and a full replacement is required at an estimated cost of $1.5 million; and 
 
Whereas, construction of a bypass road across 9 Foss Rd and removal of the bridge would result  
in significant cost savings; and 
 
Whereas, funding for construction of a bypass road was approved by City Council as part of the  
FY26 LCIP; and 
 
Whereas, the owners of 9 Foss Rd, Vineyard Christian Fellowship, have agreed to split off 1.44  
acres to sell to the City for the purposes of constructing a bypass road; and 
 
Now, T herefore, B e It Ordered by the C ity Council of the City of Lewiston  to authorize the 
acquisition of a 1.44 Acre portion of 9 Foss Rd for the agreed amount of $35,000 from the Jordan 
Rd Bridge Project (Acct# 7703 703721). 
 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD 
 
No members of the public addressed the Council at this time. 
 
REPORTS AND UPDATES 
 
Councilor Noble expressed concerns about a school bus on Marcotte Avenue and Barron Avenue 
going too fast. She noted that half of Sylvan Avenue is one way and people do not know that. 
She asked that a Council workshop be held on abandoned vehicles and the current city 
ordinance, she asked for rezoning to make the process fairer for residents who must park on the 
streets.  Councilor Nagine asked for an ordinance to address the safety of e-bikes and e-scooters, 
noting that lights should be required for nighttime operation, reflectors, etc. Read a statement 
from the Public Health Committee on the importance of childhood vaccines.  The Maine 
Resiliency Center survey closes in one week, how will the Council receive their findings? 
Councilor Martel noted the Ward 7 Meet & Greet to be held on August 20 at the Clarion Inn. 
Councilor Longchamps said she asked to have the Ethics Policy on the agenda because two local 
businesses are having a dispute and it is escalating, the Council received emails and complaints 
about comments from residents that could be harmful.
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 18, 2026 
                             
8 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
No Other Business was brought forth at this time. 
 
EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 
VOTE (309-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel: 
 
To enter into an Executive Session pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 405(6) (A) and (E) to discuss 
a legal matter with the City Attorney and an Executive Session, pursuant to MRSA Title 1, section 
405(6) (c), to discuss the acquisition or disposition of Real Estate, of which the premature 
disclosure of the information would prejudice the competitive bargaining position of the City. 
Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
Executive Session began at 8:25 pm and ended at 9:10 pm. 
  
 
VOTE (310-2026) 
Motion by Councilor Nagine, seconded by Councilor Harriman: 
 
To adjourn at 9:10 P.M.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Kathleen M. Montejo, MMC  
City Clerk 
Lewiston, Maine
